what: The verifier that `pip install uibc-core` actually gives you
why: pyproject.toml says 0.3.3 and PyPI carries 0.3.3, so the version string is not stale -- but the published verifier is not the one in this repository. Anyone who installs the package and then reads a claim about S7-S18 would be misled. This file records what was measured so the claim can be checked rather than remembered.
how_measured: downloaded the 0.3.3 sdist into a clean venv, then ran its verifier and the repository verifier on the SAME package built by tools/outsider_audit.py (build_v11 + build_ext + build_s16 + build_ckpt)
what_the_published_version_does_reproduc: the shipped fixture's verdict: INCONCLUSIVE, six checks (S1-S6)
the link1 example's three verdicts: PASS / FAIL naming file S4 / INCONCLUSIVE, matching that example's README
what_it_does_not: S7-S10 (index metadata, whole-state checkpoint, out-of-band pin, attestation closure)
S13-S18 (merkle proofs, strict base64, anchor resolution, RFC 3161, receipt chain, policy artefacts)
tools/outsider_audit.py, the outside kit, the verify endpoint, the AAC export -- none is in the sdist
limits_of_this_measurement: It measures the published checks, not the published behaviour: a check id present in both trees may still differ in what it catches.
The example runs were made against this repository's example packages, not against copies shipped in the sdist.

decisive_measurement.what: the same full-feature package (v1.1 lifecycle + merkle + anchor + RFC3161 + receipts + policies, built by tools/outsider_audit.py) fed to both verifiers

repository_result.note: S9 absent because no --expect-head was supplied

decisive_measurement.conclusion: the published verifier does not know any of S7-S18 exist; it does not merely run fewer checks on a smaller package, it cannot see the fields those checks are about
